correctness.rationale: The two masses A,C normalize and have exact mean np. The binomial probabilities increase through floor(np) and decrease from floor(np)+1 onward, forcing d_j=U(j)-Bin(j) to decrease on its left block and increase on its right. Nonzero zero-mass and zero-first-moment differences of that shape have two positive tails and one negative middle interval. Strictness follows because Bin(n,p) cannot be constant on the requisite block when n>=2. The affine-secant argument proves every convex-order inequality and all interior stop-loss comparisons. Exact-rational script verifies 11020 finite tests; the analytical proof covers all real 0<p<1 and real 0<t<n.

value.rationale: A full convex-order theorem is a mathematically motivated strict strengthening of the exact heavy-tail/variance comparison in Gross 2026. It gives all convex losses and all interior stop-loss thresholds, globally for n>=2 and every real 0<p<1, and strictly orders all mixing parameters, instead of a special numerical moment or arbitrary small slice. This answers the distributional sense in which the proposed overdispersed model is more spread than its binomial baseline.
